pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Arizona Registrar of Contractors uses PSI for trade-specific contractor examinations. Arizona applicants may be required to complete the Arizona Statutes and Rules Exam and a trade-specific examination depending on the license classification. Electrical candidates commonly prepare for classifications such as R-11 Electrical Residential, C-11 Electrical Commercial, or CR-11 Electrical Dual. Each classification has its own scope, requirements, and content outline. The PSI candidate information for Arizona contractor licensing explains that trade-specific content outlines identify the examination time limit, subject areas, number of items in each area, and reference materials. Candidates should study the content outline connected to the exact Arizona electrical classification they are pursuing. This is important because residential, commercial, and dual classifications may have different scopes and exam requirements. The Arizona R-11 Electrical Residential content outline lists 110 questions, a 70% minimum passing score, and 240 minutes of testing time.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The listed subject areas include general electrical knowledge, service feeders and branch circuits, grounding and bonding, conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, special occupancies and equipment, electrical devices, motors, low voltage, lighting, fire detection and alarm systems, safety, overcurrent protection, and photovoltaics. Because this product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code, it is designed for candidates who want to prepare using the 2026 NEC code cycle. Arizona’s official electrical exam references may vary by classification and examination update cycle. Candidates studying for an Arizona ROC electrical trade exam should match their study plan to the current PSI content outline for their selected classification while using this combo to build journeyman-level code knowledge, calculation ability, and exam readiness. Electrical exam preparation should include more than reading.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Candidates should practice locating code sections, reviewing definitions, working through tables, applying conductor and overcurrent protection rules, solving calculations, and answering timed practice questions. The stronger your code-navigation habits are before exam day, the easier it becomes to manage an open-book test under time pressure.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Arizona ROC electrical trade exams administered through PSI use approved reference materials. The Arizona R-11 Electrical Residential content outline identifies reference materials allowed in the examination center and states that candidates are responsible for bringing their own references. This makes reference familiarity a key part of preparation. Approved references may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the examination session, but candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index in the references during the examination. The PSI reference rules also state that references may not include additional loose or attached papers. Permanent tabs are allowed, while temporary removable tabs are not allowed. Open-book testing does not remove the need for strong preparation. A candidate who is unfamiliar with the code book may lose valuable time searching for basic information. A candidate who studies with the code book regularly can move faster between articles, tables, definitions, and exceptions.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is designed to support this kind of code-navigation practice. Use the NEC throughout your study sessions. When answering a practice question, locate the code rule that supports the answer. Read the entire section, check related definitions, review table notes, and look for exceptions. This habit helps candidates develop the practical code skills needed for open-book electrical exams.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Arizona electrical licensing is handled through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors rather than through a separate statewide journeyman electrician licensing board. The state licenses contracting businesses and qualifying parties for the appropriate contractor classification. Electrical candidates who want to operate as contractors or serve as qualifying parties should follow the ROC licensing path for the applicable classification. The process begins by identifying the correct license classification. Residential electrical work is associated with the R-11 Electrical classification. Commercial electrical work is associated with the C-11 Electrical classification. Dual electrical work is associated with the CR-11 Electrical classification. The selected classification determines the scope of work, required examinations, and application path. Arizona ROC applicants must complete the examination requirements for the license classification unless an approved waiver applies.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The PSI candidate information explains that exam requirements must be completed by the person who will act as the qualifying party. The qualifying party is the individual whose experience and examination record support the license application. After completing the required examination or examinations, applicants submit the completed license application and original score report to the Arizona Registrar of Contractors for processing within the required time period. Licensing applications are not accepted until the examination requirements have been completed. Candidates should keep copies of their score reports, experience records, and application materials. The Application Service included with this Ultimate Combo is designed to support candidates through the administrative side of the process. The exam prep materials support study and technical readiness, while the Application Service helps candidates stay organized as they work through paperwork, classification selection, and licensing documentation.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Arizona regulates electrical contracting through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. The state’s contractor licensing structure focuses on business licensing and qualifying parties rather than issuing one universal statewide journeyman electrician license. Candidates working toward electrical contractor licensing should identify the correct ROC classification and follow the current requirements for that classification. Electrical contractor classifications are based on the type of work being performed. Residential electrical contractors, commercial electrical contractors, and dual electrical contractors have different license classifications. The license classification determines the authorized scope of work and the trade exam content outline that applies to the qualifying party. For Arizona ROC licensing, the qualifying party is central to the application process. This individual must meet the experience and examination requirements for the license classification.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: The qualifying party is responsible for demonstrating the trade knowledge and experience needed to support the license application. The Arizona ROC candidate information explains that applicants should use the License Classification Requirements form to determine which examination or examinations are required. Trade exams are scheduled through PSI, and certain applicants may also need to complete the Arizona Statutes and Rules Exam. Exam waiver conditions may apply in specific circumstances, but those are handled through the ROC licensing process. Because Arizona’s system is contractor-classification based, candidates should avoid assuming that a “journeyman electrician license” means the same thing in Arizona that it means in another state. In Arizona, journeyman-level preparation is valuable for trade competency, field advancement, and electrical contractor exam readiness, but the state licensing path is organized around ROC contractor classifications.

pieces.h: State Requirements

The R-11 Electrical Residential classification applies to residential electrical work. The C-11 Electrical Commercial classification applies to commercial electrical work. The CR-11 Electrical Dual classification is associated with both residential and commercial electrical work. Candidates should select the classification that matches the scope of work they plan to contract for in Arizona. The C-11 Electrical Commercial scope includes installation, alteration, and repair of wiring, related electrical material, and equipment used in generating, transmitting, or utilizing electrical energy less than 600 volts.

pieces.t: Arizona does not use one single statewide master electrician license structure like some states. Arizona regulates electrical contracting through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors.

pieces.h: Q: Who administers Arizona electrical contractor licensing?
pieces.t: Arizona electrical contractor licensing is administered through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors.

pieces.h: Q: Who administers Arizona electrical contractor exams?
pieces.t: Arizona Registrar of Contractors examinations are administered through PSI for applicants taking Arizona ROC contractor exams.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam?
pieces.t: The AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam is listed as 110 questions.

pieces.h: Q: How much time is allowed for the AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam?
pieces.t: The AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam is listed with a 240-minute time limit.

pieces.h: Q: What score is required to pass the AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam?
pieces.t: The AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam is listed with a 70% minimum passing score.

pieces.h: Q: What topics are on the AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam?
pieces.t: Topics include general electrical knowledge, service feeders and branch circuits, grounding and bonding, conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, special occupancies and equipment, devices, motors, low voltage, lighting, illuminated signs, fire detection and alarm systems, safety, overcurrent protection, and photovoltaics.

pieces.h: Q: Can Arizona C-11 or CR-11 applicants use the NASCLA electrical exam?
pieces.t: Arizona exam information identifies that C-11 and CR-11 Electrical Commercial applicants may choose between the NASCLA Accredited Trade Examination for Electrical Contractors and the AZ ROC Electrical Commercial exam.

pieces.h: Q: Can I use temporary tabs during an Arizona PSI exam?
pieces.t: No. Arizona PSI reference rules allow permanent tabs only. Temporary tabs, including Post-it notes or other removable tabs, are not allowed.

pieces.h: Q: Can I write in my references during the Arizona PSI exam?
pieces.t: No. Approved references may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the examination, but candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index references during the examination session.

pieces.h: Q: Why does this Super Combo include the 2026 NEC?
pieces.t: This Super Combo is based on the 2026 NEC for students who want current-code study materials, stronger code navigation practice, and a newer NEC reference as part of their preparation routine.

pieces.h: Q: Why does this combo include an Electrician Calculations Study Guide?
pieces.t: The calculations guide helps students practice electrical math, formula selection, load calculations, conductor sizing, service and feeder work, branch-circuit calculations, motors, and other math-based advanced electrical preparation topics.

pieces.h: Q: How should I study with this Super Combo?
pieces.t: Use the Arizona Master Electrician Study Guide to organize your review, the Electrician Calculations Study Guide to practice math-based problems, the NEC 2026 paperback with tabs to build code navigation skills, and the flash cards for quick daily review.

pieces.h: Q: What is included in this Arizona Master Electrician combo?
pieces.t: This combo includes the 2026 Arizona Master Electrician Study Guide and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs. It is designed to support electrical exam preparation, NEC study, and organized code-book review.

pieces.h: Q: Does Arizona have a statewide master electrician license?
pieces.t: Arizona licenses electrical work through contractor classifications administered by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Electrical candidates commonly prepare for residential, commercial, or dual electrical contractor classifications instead of a separate statewide master electrician license format used in some other states.

pieces.h: Q: Is the Arizona electrical trade exam open book?
pieces.t: Yes. Arizona electrical trade examinations administered through PSI allow approved reference materials in the examination center. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references and following PSI’s reference rules.

pieces.h: Q: Are NEC tabs allowed during the Arizona electrical exam?
pieces.t: PSI allows references to be tabbed or indexed with permanent tabs only. Permanent tabs are tabs that would tear the page if removed. Temporary or removable tabs are not allowed.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the Arizona C-11 or CR-11 Electrical Commercial exam?
pieces.t: PSI lists the Arizona C-11 and CR-11 Electrical Commercial exam as 110 questions with a minimum passing score of 70% and a time allowance of 240 minutes.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the Arizona R-11 Electrical Residential exam?
pieces.t: PSI lists the Arizona R-11 Electrical Residential exam as 110 questions with a minimum passing score of 70% and a time allowance of 240 minutes.

pieces.h: Q: Does this product include the NEC book?
pieces.t: Yes. This product includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs along with the 2026 Arizona Master Electrician Study Guide.

pieces.h: Q: Can this combo help with code-book navigation?
pieces.t: Yes. The NEC paperback and tabs are useful for practicing code-book navigation. Students can use the tabs to organize major sections and practice locating rules, definitions, tables, and related code provisions during study sessions.

pieces.h: Q: Does this study guide guarantee a passing score?
pieces.t: No. This combo is a study and preparation resource. It helps organize review and code practice, but passing depends on the candidate’s knowledge, preparation, test performance, and compliance with Arizona and PSI requirements.
